10.1016_j.cej.2026.176647: The corrosion resistance behavior of High-Entropy Metallic Glasses (HE-MGs) has received extensive attention and research due to its wide range of engineering applications. However, research on the relationship between high-entropy properties and corrosion properties is limited, leaving uncertainty about how configurational entropy and high-entropy characteristics affect the corrosion resistance of materials. In this paper, the corrosion behavior of three typical Pd-based Metallic Glasses (MGs) with different entropy values in 0.5 M H 2 SO 4 was investigated. The results show that the self-corrosion current density of Pd-based HE-MG is about 0.3% of that of ternary Pd-based MG with a smaller configurational entropy, which is a large improvement in the corrosion resistance. XPS studies show that the content of Pd in Pd-based HE-MG is only 50% of other Pd-based MGs, but it has the highest increment of Pd oxide after corrosion. The oxide films formed in ternary and quaternary Pd-based MGs are unstable while the Pd-based HE-MG forms a highly stable oxide film that is not prone to dissolution. Moreover, the binding energy was used to directly correlate the corrosion resistance of the material with the stability of the material itself and the surface films. These findings provide a new perspective for subsequent research on regulating the corrosion resistance of MGs through configurational entropy control of high-entropy characteristics. • The different corrosion mechanisms of 3 Pd-based MGs in H 2 SO 4 solution were revealed. • The oxide films formed by Pd 40 Ni 40 P 20 MG and Pd 40 Cu 30 Ni 10 P 20 MG are unstable. • Pd 20 Pt 20 Cu 20 Ni 20 P 20 HE-MG forms a single, uniform and stable oxide film. • The binding energy correlates the corrosion resistance with the oxide stability. • Configurational entropy has a positive effect on the anti-corrosion behavior of MGs.
10.1016_j.ejrh.2026.103895: Accurate flow prediction is essential for effective water resources management. Influenced by meteorological events, watershed characteristics, and natural geographical conditions, daily runoff process exhibits sharp fluctuations in flow. Despite advances in deep learning (DL) methods through specialized strategies for extreme flow prediction, their performance remains limited. Methods that modify loss functions often focus on either extreme floods or droughts, and such approaches typically compromise accuracy for normal flows. Moreover, gating-based multi-predictor combination strategies inappropriately incorporate meteorological forcings and lack a process-based understanding of the dominant hydrological drivers, thereby limiting their ability to identify extreme events. To mitigate these problems, we propose a Deep Process Learning-Long Short-term Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (DPL-LSTKAN). Specifically, DPL-LSTKAN captures the temporal evolution of meteorological forcings and uses Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (KAN) to capture the intrinsic dependencies between meteorological forcings and runoff. A decoupled learning scheme is adopted to separately represent extreme and normal flows. In addition, a physics-guided gating mechanism dynamically assigns predictor weights in accordance with dominant hydrological processes. Experiments in the Upper Hanjiang River Basin (UHRB) demonstrate that: (a) DPL-LSTKAN substantially outperforms state-of-the-art baseline models across short- to medium-term lead times, with Root Mean Square Error reduction of 4%-10%; (b) DPL-LSTKAN improves flow prediction for both extreme event (an average improvement of 28%) while maintaining accuracy for normal flow regimes; (c) DPL-LSTKAN mitigates the underestimation of flood peaks and produces drought predictions that align more closely with physical hydrological constraints. This study highlights a promising pathway to enhance the predictability of both extreme floods and droughts.
10.1016_j.porgcoat.2026.110428: Waterborne (WB) epoxy-amine coatings rely on the incorporation of coalescing agents to achieve proper film formation, yet their specific roles in the thermal evolution, curing behavior, and barrier performance of these systems remain insufficiently understood. In this study, four coalescing agents, including propylene glycol (PG), dipropylene glycol n-butyl ether (DPnB), ethylene glycol butyl ether (EGBE), and butyl glycol acetate (BGA), were incorporated at concentrations ranging from 0.5 to 25 wt% (based on binder solids) to systematically investigate their influence on film formation and coating performance. Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) of the as-dried base component was used to determine the glass transition temperature (T g ) associated with minimum film forming temperature (MFFT) behavior, while DSC of fully cured films was used to evaluate network development and residual plasticization. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) was performed to evaluate water uptake, dielectric properties, and barrier performance as a function of coalescent type and loading. In addition, an EIS-based two-electrode sensor configuration was used to monitor impedance and capacitance continuously during the transition from wet coating to a fully cured film. The results show that coalescent physicochemical properties strongly influence both film formation dynamics and final barrier performance. Moderate coalescent additions improved particle deformation and coating impedance, whereas excessive loading increased water uptake and reduced coating resistance due to residual plasticization. Among the investigated systems, PG showed minimal long-term plasticization and favorable barrier properties at low concentrations, while DPnB exhibited pronounced concentration-dependent effects associated with higher retention in the polymer phase.
